PullRequest.Title: sessions: add cloud automation repository store
PullRequest.Body:
Refs #337478. Part 2 of the cloud automations stack, based on #339181.

### Changes
- Adds an inert, provider-local `CloudAutomationStore` that caches user-owned cloud automation definitions from known and recent Agents Window private/internal GitHub.com repositories.
- Refreshes only on explicit request; coalesces concurrent refreshes and retains a repository's previous definitions if its refresh fails.
- Persists only account-scoped repository references. Account changes, sign-out and disposal cancel in-flight work and clear cached definitions.
- Also includes `a760d027cd8`, a 3-line browser fallback test wording cleanup not yet on the base branch.

Provider registration, mutations, history and UI remain deferred.

### Validation
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\providers\copilotChatSessions\test\browser\cloudAutomationStore.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\providers\copilotChatSessions\test\browser\cloudAutomationApiClient.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\github\test\browser\githubApiClient.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\services\request\test\browser\requestService.test.ts --reporter dot` — passed (118 tests).
- `npm run typecheck-client` and `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed.
- Targeted ESLint, formatter verification and commit hooks — passed.
- Read-only correctness and security reviews found no actionable issues.

Scenarios.Scenario: Store construction, cache observation, account changes, sign-out, and disposal
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Construction registers one account-change listener and synchronously resets observables; account changes and disposal cancel the current token source and clear in-memory entries. No network, filesystem, subprocess, database, or IPC work must complete, and the new store has no production importer or constructor in this PR.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant work per lifecycle event plus clearing the single cached-entry array reference; definitions are not traversed during reset/disposal.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No asynchronous work is started. Existing in-flight requests are cancelled through one lifetime token source.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Construction starts with an empty cache. Account changes, sign-out, and disposal invalidate all in-memory definitions; no automatic refresh or polling occurs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: repository-wide symbol search found only the added class, its tests, and documentation, with no production import or instantiation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for the current diff because the class is production-unreachable; future provider registration is explicitly deferred.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds no startup or account-change boundary work and currently exposes no user-reachable performance path.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: If a future caller invokes registration, one GitHub repository visibility request must finish before the account-scoped repository reference is read, merged, serialized, and stored. This method is not called by production code in this PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authenticated GET /repos/{owner}/{name} to verify private visibility
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one request per registration invocation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No store registration workflow existed in the base; this PR adds the method but does not connect a production caller.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read, parse, merge, JSON-stringify, and store account-scoped repository references in profile machine storage
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full stored-reference read and one full serialization/write per successful registration
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No cloud-automation repository-reference storage existed in the base.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs after visibility verification before registration resolves

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One repository per invocation; persisted references grow with distinct successful registrations, but there is no production registration surface in this change.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Independent registration calls are not coalesced or globally limited; each individual call performs one visibility request. No realistic production concurrency exists in this diff because there are no callers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Visibility is not cached. Successful registration merges the reference into profile-local machine storage; definitions remain unfetched. Cold and repeated registrations each perform the same visibility request.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the boundary and cardinality; high that it is currently production-unreachable.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Future UI frequency and number of explicitly registered repositories are unknown, but no current product workflow can trigger the method.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The one-request-per-explicit-registration cost is bounded, and the diff does not wire a user-reachable trigger.

Scenarios.Scenario: Explicit cloud-automation catalogue refresh through GitHubCloudAutomationStore.refresh
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A future explicit caller would synchronously read stored references and at most 10 Agents-owned recent workspaces, then sequentially verify visibility and list definitions for each effective deduplicated repository. Results publish only after all repositories and the final storage write complete. There is no production caller or store construction in this PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and JSON-parse account-scoped repository references from profile storage
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One stored-reference parse per refresh, plus one additional parse before the final merged persistence write
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No cloud-automation repository cache or refresh workflow existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initial read precedes network discovery; the final read/serialization precedes refresh completion

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve Agents-owned recent workspace records through registered session providers
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most 10 stored recent workspaces, then deduplicated by lower-cased owner/name
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The recent-workspace service existed, but cloud-automation refresh did not invoke it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous discovery occurs before network refresh; includeVSCodeRecents=false avoids workspace-file filesystem reads

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authenticated GitHub visibility GET followed by Copilot automation list pagination and optional definition-detail GETs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For R effective repositories: R visibility requests plus 1-10 list page requests per eligible repository and up to one detail request per summary lacking a prompt; repositories are serial, details are limited to five
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The API client existed on the base, but no store invoked these operations as a catalogue refresh and no production caller is added by this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All repository requests are on the refresh critical path before entries publish

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Flatten cached definitions into a new published array and JSON-stringify merged repository references
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Linear in cached definitions and known repository references once per completed refresh
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small synchronous finalization after network operations and before observers receive the completed snapshot

Scenarios.ScalingInput: R effective deduplicated repositories: up to 10 recent entries plus distinct persisted registrations. For each repository, one visibility request precedes one to 10 paginated list requests; summaries missing prompts can add one detail request each, limited to five concurrently within a repository.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Concurrent refresh() calls coalesce through refreshPromise. Repositories are processed serially. Within CloudAutomationApiClient.list, page requests are serial and detail requests are limited to five; account reset can cancel an old refresh before a new explicit refresh starts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm entries are retained only as failure fallback and do not suppress visibility/list requests; every explicit refresh revalidates all effective repositories. Successful empty results replace prior entries. Failures retain each repository's prior definitions. There is no negative cache, but no polling or automatic retry exists.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for serial network fan-out, cardinality bounds for recent workspaces, coalescing, and warm-cache behavior; high that production reachability is absent.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Future wiring could make additive per-repository latency noticeable, especially with persisted repositories or paginated catalogues, but this PR is explicitly inert and supplies no realistic user trigger from which to establish impact.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression in this diff. Although a future caller may need to revisit serial all-repository refresh latency, performance impact is not user-reachable until a later change wires the store.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and every diff page. The production addition is an explicitly invoked, lifecycle-cancelled cache with bounded recent-workspace discovery and coalesced refreshes, but it has no production importer, registration, or caller in this PR. Network and profile-storage costs were traced for future registration/refresh paths; no high-confidence user-visible performance regression is introduced, and this PR does not fix a provable prior performance regression.
